newsitem.title: CHINA: China said in need of financial futures.
newsitem.headline: China said in need of financial futures.

text.p: China should move quickly to develop financial futures to offset risks in treasury bonds, stocks and foreign exchange trading, a senior financial expert and lawmaker was quoted as saying on Friday.

"In addition to its commodity futures, (China) should also launch financial futures as early as possible," the Futures Herald said, quoting Dong Fureng of the National People's Congress, or parliament.
China already allows trading in a number of commodity futures products.

But China banned trade of its sole financial futures product -- treasury bond futures -- in May 1995 after major irregularities left traders with huge losses and one brokerage was forced to merge to avoid failure.

Domestic treasury bond underwriters should have a market to hedge their risks due to rising amounts of state debt being issued, said Dong, vice chairman of parliament's financial and economic committee.
China issued a record 195.257 billion yuan ($23.5 billion) of government debt in 1996, up 27 percent over the previous year, official figures showed.
A listing of domestic stock index futures would help traders offset risks in share trading, he said.
Trading of foreign exchange futures would provide a hedging mechanism for China to improve management of its mounting foreign exchange reserves, he said.
China's foreign exchange reserves hit $110 billion by the end of February, Dai Xianglong, governor of the central bank, said in Hong Kong on Friday.
